VibePascal v58 -- aarch64-linux NATIVE compiler (runs on ARM64 Linux, e.g. a
64-bit Raspberry Pi).  A .ppu shorter than its own header says is truncated, and
a half-written one can no longer hang the compiler.
Source commit: dedf242c696a543f9626e2839ced40876478a98a
Parent release for THIS target: v56 (a187bbac34)
Built: 2026-09-11, cross-built on x86_64-linux via a freshly bootstrapped
       compiler/ppcrossa64 (md5 eab972e2457f458e0c42bd2a51afa4d6, itself built
       from a CLEAN unit tree by the v58 native ppcx64,
       md5 8c8179b2f0a452cebec0131aa301b076)
Binary: bin/ppca64  md5 78c729e8addfb7a8e80ddb245ca57049
                    sha256 d5d6e998ede92c89bf25d88263e8eae4aae5b18fb99f26bcc2dc828a37a49c7f
                    5181472 bytes, ELF 64-bit ARM aarch64, statically linked, stripped

THIS TARGET SKIPPED v57.  x86_64 shipped v57 and v58 on 2026-09-11 while ARM
stayed at v56, so this release carries BOTH .ppu reader fixes, not one:

  v57 (c31227c8ca)  a half-written .ppu is an ERROR, not an infinite 99%-CPU spin
                    with no message.  On the v56 binary this replaces, a killed
                    build or a full disk could hang a compile forever.
  v58 (dedf242c69)  a .ppu SHORTER than the length its own header declares is
                    rejected instead of silently accepted.  v57 only noticed
                    damage it happened to trip over; lose the TAIL of a unit and
                    there was nothing to trip over, so the compiler built your
                    program against a unit that is not all there -- exit 0, no
                    message, nothing to search a log for.

THIS DOES NOT TURN GOOD BUILDS RED.  The rejection is soft and self-healing: a
truncated unit whose source is available is RECOMPILED and the build goes green;
a good copy in a later -Fu directory is used instead; only a truncated unit with
no source and no other copy stops the compile, and it stops with the message an
absent unit already gives.  Nobody is ever told to go and delete a file.

COMPILER BINARY ONLY.  No RTL change, no package change, no PPU FORMAT change
between v56 and v58 -- the reader got stricter, the format did not move.  An
existing aarch64-linux unit set stays valid and does not need rebuilding.

VERIFIED ON THESE EXACT BYTES
-----------------------------
  * dist/ppu-truncation-check.sh ppca64 aarch64-linux, against the real
    55282-byte packages/aspell/units/aarch64-linux/aspelldyn.ppu:
        11/25 offsets clean, 14 problem(s), exit 1   on the v56 binary this replaces
        25/25 offsets clean,  0 problem(s), exit 0   on this one
    Of the 14: 9 truncations HUNG and had to be killed at 30s, and 5 were
    ACCEPTED with rc=0 -- a corrupt unit taken as valid, silently.
    The pre-fix binary is the one that actually shipped as v56
    (md5 96241cbc8871786eb790c3c068258e33), preserved and re-run this cycle
    under emulation -- not a reconstruction, and not an argument from source.
  * EXECUTION, not inspection.  This binary RUNS: qemu-aarch64-static reports
    version 3.3.1, and it compiled and ran
        tests/test/tinlinevarnativeint1.pp -Munleashed -> VERDICT:PASS
        tests/test/tblockscopefinal1.pp                -> MATRIX: PASS
                                     (all corners block-scoped, released exactly once)
  * dist/arm-runtime-proof.sh exercises this tarball end to end and checks the
    md5 above against the bytes it unpacks, so the number in this file cannot
    drift from the artifact without the proof failing.

NOT PROVEN HERE, AND SAID PLAINLY: qemu-user is an emulator.  It runs the real
shipped bytes and real aarch64 instruction encodings, so codegen and RTL defects
DO surface -- but it is not a Raspberry Pi.  NOBODY HAS RUN ANY VIBEPASCAL
RELEASE ON PHYSICAL ARM SILICON.  Do not quote a pass here as a hardware
sign-off.
